newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian wool price to rise in 1997/98 - ABARE.
newsitem.headline: Australian wool price to rise in 1997/98 - ABARE.

text.p: Australian wool prices are expected to rise 6.6 percent in 1997/98 (June 30) to average 650 cents a kg clean, based on the eastern market indicator, the Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics (ABARE) said in its June quarter review on Tuesday.
ABARE, the Australian government's key commodities forecaster, said shorn wool production was forecast to rise by nearly one percent in 1997/98 to 688,000 tonnes.
The forecasts are steady with ABARE's March projections.

Despite increased competition from other fibres, demand for raw wool was expected to rise as a result of higher economic growth and increased consumer spending in key wool consuming countries particularly the United States and United Kingdom.

While subdued consumer spending was likely to limit the extent of growth in key western European countries, processing stocks were at low levels and positive growth in retail demand could prompt relatively quick higher raw wool demand, it said.
Rising retail demand in the major wool consuming countries of Asia was also expected to increase, but higher stocks were likely to limit the rate of demand for raw wool, it said.

"Reflecting market uncertainty and ongoing changes in factors affecting demand and supply, it is estimated the average price has a 75 percent probability of being in the range 620-715 cents a kg," ABARE said in its Australian Commodities review.

ABARE said that despite the small increase in forecast wool production, sales from the Wool International stockpile and from privately held stocks would be the main influence on the quantity of wool available for sale in 1997/98.

Mixed livestock-crop producers, who hold the largest proportion of private stocks, were likely to continue to reduce stocks of wool to maintain farm incomes because returns from cropping were expected to be lower in 1997/98, ABARE said.
It said sheep numbers were expected to continue to rise, up 1.6 percent in 1997/98 to around 124 million in March 1998.

Following a strong recovery in 1996/97, Australian wool exports were expected to remain flat in 1997/98 at 840,000 tonnes, with higher production and increased sales from private stocks being offset by a 15 percent forecast drop in Wool International sales.
ABARE said exports to western Europe were likely to rise as a result of restocking but to fall slightly to China, Taiwan and other south east Asian countries with rising domestic stocks.
